content: The test image shows an open soybean pod with a seed surrounded by fluffy white cottony mycelium/mold growth. The pod walls appear darkened. Top candidates: **White Mold** (cottony white mycelial growth inside pods) and **Downy_mildew** (whitish fungal mass inside pods/seeds). Let me check references.

The test image clearly shows an open soybean pod with fluffy white cottony mycelium surrounding the seed, with dark spots on the pod wall (consistent with sclerotia). This is highly characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).

Key evidence:
- Fluffy white cottony mycelial growth inside the pod around the seed
- Dark spots/marks on the pod wall (likely sclerotia)
- Pod split open, consistent with White Mold pod infection
- White Mold description: "pods contain smaller, lighter, cottony seeds; infected seeds may be flat, shriveled, or replaced by sclerotia"

Downy Mildew was ruled out — its reference shows only leaf symptoms, and its pod symptoms are described as "crusty/dried" not fluffy/cottony. Phomopsis shows circular dark pycnidia on pods, no cottony growth. Anthracnose shows dark lesions with setae.
